subject: Daz
fact: Daz is currently very small, very angry, and in the party's possession; he is a drow whose House T'sarran has vowed vengeance; he responds to threats with minimal affect, saying 'Tiny, tiny little vengeance.'
source_quote: This is highly irregular, and House T'sarran will have its vengeance!

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is reportedly very confused about the concept of a library with effectively infinite capacity; he does not understand why books aren't donated until questions can be asked indefinitely; he believes cute googly eyes make others perceive him more favorably, and can produce proliferating eyes to demonstrate his true nature as an ooze with multi-sensory perception.
source_quote: I can actually see different ways. This is how ooze work. But I discovered that if you have these cute eyes, people take you more friendly.

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader received all five books with barely-contained delight; she reveres the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal as a masterpiece and maintains a collection of drow prison journals; she assigns scholars to specific threads and is open to being interviewed directly as a primary source.
source_quote: This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece of interesting value. I can't wait to study it carefully.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is practical and perceptive; she suggested the party be interviewed instead of reading books; she identified Daz as a drow in their possession; she delivered a merciless response to the spy's request for a question; she accepted the assignment to couples counseling with Dawnbringer with clear relief.
source_quote: You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is an elderly half-elf scholar with a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts; he is frantic and outraged that the First Reader did not inform him of the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut; his quiet niche became suddenly significant after Stroud beat Protanther at chess.
source_quote: I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an avowed scholar assigned to the Jimjar thread, which dovetailed with an avowed named Khell-Vire interested in a specific subject — not the party generally, but the narrator in particular.
source_quote: Zalthir wanted to know about Jimjar.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts; he has a tremendous track record in resolving interpersonal conflict issues of sentient artifacts; he was assigned to Thorin and Dawnbringer for couples counseling.
source_quote: an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in working through the interpersonal conflict issues of the sentient artifact.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a drow house that has vowed vengeance against Daz, a member of the party who is currently in their possession; their threat is delivered with ceremonial gravity but met with Daz's dismissive tone.
source_quote: This is highly irregular, and House T'sarran will have its vengeance!

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed are scholars and sages of Candlekeep who assign questions in exchange for books; they maintain specialized threads (e.g., Jimjar, Khell-Vire) and prioritize individual-focused inquiry over general party observation; they operate with ritualized precision and academic hierarchy.
source_quote: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular.

subject: book exchange
fact: Five books were donated to the First Reader, triggering the assignment of scholars to specific threads; each book corresponded to one question, and the exchange activated a cascade of academic interest in the party members, particularly the narrator and Daz.

subject: arrival of the cleric of Bahamut
fact: The arrival of a cleric of Bahamut — the narrator — triggered a frantic intervention by Vareth, a half-elf scholar whose decades-long niche in half-orc Bahamut converts became suddenly relevant; this event was perceived as academically significant only after Stroud beat Protanther at chess.
source_quote: I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Stroud beats Protanther at chess
fact: Stroud's victory over Protanther at chess acted as an unexpected catalyst that elevated the academic relevance of niche studies, particularly Vareth's work on half-orc Bahamut converts, transforming a quiet specialty into a matter of urgent scholarly interest.
source_quote: And then Stroud beat Protanther at chess.

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is a revered artifact held by the First Reader; it is considered a masterpiece of drow prison writing and is part of an established collection of drow prison journals.
source_quote: This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece of interesting value.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The spy demanded information about the prayer beads, a bold request given their current status as an unbook-donating captive; this request was immediately denied by Thorin.
source_quote: The spy's voice came out approximately at the volume of an extremely annoyed insect.

subject: Khell-Vire and the narrator
fact: Khell-Vire, an avowed scholar, is interested in a specific subject — not the party generally, but the narrator in particular — which was assigned to Zalthir as part of the Jimjar thread; this indicates the narrator is a subject of unique academic fascination.
source_quote: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular.

subject: Dawnbringer and Thorin
fact: Dawnbringer and Thorin are assigned to Philemon for couples counseling, indicating their relationship is recognized as a sentient artifact with interpersonal conflict requiring psychological preservation and historical cataloging.
source_quote: I'm all up for couples counseling with Dawnbringer.

subject: after Stroud beats Protanther at chess
fact: The event of Stroud beating Protanther at chess serves as a temporal anchor that reconfigured academic priorities, making previously obscure studies suddenly urgent and relevant.
source_quote: And then Stroud beat Protanther at chess.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze entity capable of producing proliferating eyes; he presents himself with affectations of cute googly eyes to appear more approachable, but his true perception is multi-sensory; he is not a threat but a being whose scale of perception exceeds the comprehension of others.
source_quote: I can actually see different ways. This is how ooze work.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an academic sanctuary where knowledge is exchanged for books, and scholars (the Avowed) are assigned to specialized threads; it operates with ritualized hierarchy and intense focus on individual narratives over collective ones.
source_quote: the sages, the professors — providing more books will get you more FaceTime.
